status: prospective browser acceptance protocol; no execution results in this file
beneficiary: The same existing FieldJourney browser consumer and unchanged authoritative owners.
question: Can optional focused stage navigation expose one chosen task surface while preserving the complete same-person paid journey and current observation/keyboard boundaries?
baseline: The existing page exposes identity preparation, local workshop, assembly and road in one long simultaneous workflow. Its actual command routing, owner facts and full-view behavior already operate.
hypothesis: A presentation-only chosen-stage view can reduce simultaneously exposed task surfaces to one without changing authoritative state, hiding current committed identity/receipt, or allowing hidden-road keys to act.
rivals: An apparent simplification could conceal earned amendment or the next actual owner action.
Navigation could accidentally issue commands, replace a snapshot, infer availability, or replay a held key.
Passing DOM presence checks could conceal CSS-visible historical/active facts or a false readiness caption.
A successful scripted route does not establish improved human comprehension, speed, accessibility or preference.

contract.default: Existing full view remains the default and preserves all original gameplay controls.
contract.focused: Optional local presentation selects identity, workshop, assembly or road. Selection supplies no gameplay permission and sends no owner command.
contract.authority: Read all readiness, costs, completion, pending identity, custody and historical status from the actual current owner snapshot. A suggested stage is not permission or automatically executed action.
contract.always_visible: Current committed identity/status and actual latest receipt/connection state remain visible when a task surface is hidden.
contract.history: After departure, workshop facts remain explicitly historical; visiting that view cannot suggest live worker presence or reopen preparation.
contract.amendment: Between encounters, earned allocation and explicit identity review/confirmation remain reachable; pending amendments are not silently confirmed or discarded.
contract.keyboard: Leaving/hiding the road disarms road keyboard input. Returning requires actual deliberate focus and a fresh released key. Held/interrupted input cannot queue or bypass neutral-release quarantine.
contract.terminal: Complete and withdrawn boundaries remain authoritative; navigation or reads cannot restart, heal, refund, grant XP or fabricate return/delivery.

acceptance.measure: Repeated local stage changes, full/focused toggles and ordinary reads send zero POST commands and preserve exact owner snapshot/sequence.
Actual Chromium computed visibility exposes exactly the selected task group in focused mode; default full mode exposes all groups. DOM presence alone is insufficient.
Each focused group retains the actual same committed person and latest accepted/refused receipt, including historical departure facts.

Execute an entire real two-encounter route through focused visible controls and compare exact final owner state with an equivalent full-view pointer command sequence. Preserve two rig consumptions, costs, progression, identity and real completion.

Actual survey victory remains nonfinal; navigate to preparation, allocate actually earned points, explicitly review/confirm an eligible earned amendment, and return to the real remaining encounter without grants/refunds.
Focus the road, hide it through navigation, press mapped keys and verify zero POST and exact unchanged owner state. Return alone cannot arm; fresh actual surface focus and released press can act.
Hold a mapped key across road hiding/return; key repeats and another mapped key cannot act until actual neutral release, then a fresh focused press delegates one existing command.
Retain existing lost/delayed accepted-response quarantine and explicit read recovery without replay; navigation cannot clear uncertainty or consume queued input.
Visit workshop after departure, and all views after withdrawal/completion. Check truthful historical/terminal text, no live worker picture, and no new paid mutation/refund/return.

An isolated actual renderer mutation that labels an unconfirmed/pending identity or unfunded entry as ready must be rejected by the same visible-state oracle. Retain mutant bytes and detection evidence.
Run the existing maximal Field wrapper and keyboard/withdrawal browser instruments when their UI/dependency closures change. Preserve command bodies, fixtures and timeouts.

Fingerprint the actual app/HTML/CSS/protocol/producer/compiled host and applicable owner/dependency closure before and after execution. A changed source is refused or reported as superseded, never relabelled current.

analysis: Compare exact scripted deterministic states and actual POST traces; do not treat multiple checks/screenshots/views as independent participants or measured effort. Report any unsuccessful route, hidden necessary control, false-ready result or source change.
execution_limits: Use the repository pinned SDK/browser contracts, bounded owned hosts and external scratch output. No auto retry after an established policy denial; no changed game rule, comparison, fixture, timeout or security gate to obtain a pass.
nonclaims: No human usability, accessibility, onboarding success, speedup, reduced cognitive load or preference measured.
No Unity Editor/API/IL2CPP, Windows Player, Steam, physical-device or ordinary-user validation.
No new gameplay owner, application, save, account, recipient package or consumed historical capability.
No NPC presence, home return, delivery or reward inferred from local navigation.

brain_contribution.SCI-013: Explicit rivals separate apparent surface simplification from hidden actionable state.
brain_contribution.SCI-014: Computed visibility and scripted route parity operationalize software presentation correctness, not human comprehension.
brain_contribution.SCI-017: Same exact command sequence and owner-state comparison isolate presentation from gameplay rules.
brain_contribution.SCI-061: Human usability/accessibility claims require actual appropriate participants and devices.
